unmapped_findings: Fe-30Mn-1.2C-4Al is one of the intermediate Al variants (2–6 wt.% Al). Its mechanical data are only very weakly affected by the applied aging treatments, in contrast to Fe-30Mn-1.2C (weakening/embrittlement on aging) and Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al (strengthening on aging).
Intermediate alloy variants with 2–6 wt.% Al do not show equivalent mechanical properties compared with the ~8 wt.% Al variant, and show a much smaller influence of aging on the tensile behavior.

For compositions with 25–30 wt.% Mn and up to 4–5 wt.% Al (when naturally aged), the TWIP effect prevails; after aging at 500–600 °C, twinning is reduced and strain hardening is essentially associated with κ-carbide and solid-solution strengthening.

Al below 5 wt.% gives a single austenite phase at room temperature; Al promotes nanoprecipitates upon aging with L′1₂ structure and approximate (Fe,Mn)₃AlC stoichiometry (κ-carbides, non-oxide perovskites); κ-carbides have <3% lattice mismatch with the austenitic Fe-Mn-C matrix and can form cuboidal nanoprecipitates.
κ-carbides form either at 500–600 °C or during quenching for >10 wt.% Al; the nm-sized κ-carbides are thermally very stable at 600 °C and prevail after 100 h with only modest coarsening.
Fe-Mn-Al-C austenitic steels enable density reductions up to 18%, but no specific mass density value is reported for Fe-30Mn-1.2C-4Al.
